newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - July 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - July 14.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY
- State Council urges all areas to carry out grain purchasing policy.
- Sichuan provincial government holds a meeting to discuss ways to lighten farmers' financial burden and bans state measures requiring farmers' labour or money.
XINHUA DAILY TELEGRAPH
- Henan province's summer grain production hits a record high of about 24 million tonnes, an increase of 3.2 million tonnes over last year.
CHINA SECURITIES
- Shanghai exports hit $13.952 billion in first half, up 29 percent, while imports hit $10.5 billion, down 8.1 percent year-on-year.
- China to continue to limit production and export of tungsten, tin and antimony in 1997.
INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS DAILY
- China Baotou Iron and Steel Co exports hit $64.38 million in first half, completing 1997 target.
- China to invest 777 million yuan to build Yangpu port in Hainan.
FUTURES HERALD
- China reiterates ban on overseas futures trade as government says new wave of illegal trading emerges.
- Central bank aims to trim non-performing loans by 2-3 percent.
ECONOMIC INFORMATION DAILY
- State Science and Technology Commission issues guidelines on transfer of state personnel with technical secrets.
ECONOMIC DAILY
- Tax authorities consider six percent tax on 90 octane and 12 percent tax on 70 octane.
CHINA BUSINESS DAILY
- State Grain Reserve Administration calls on local officials to guard against rain damage to grain and oil reserves.
MARKET DAILY
- Hot weather in Beijing boosts sales of air conditioners.
- Sales of light duty vehicles rise in January-April.
- China mobile phone users are expected to exceed 10 million by end 1997.
FINANCIAL NEWS
- Bank of China Group sees Hong Kong economic growth at 5.8 percent in second half.
CHINA DAILY
- China suspends diplomatic relations with Sao Tome and Principe for establishing diplomatic ties with Taiwan.
- China's industrial and commercial tax revenues maintain fast growth in the first half and complete more than half the year's tax target.
- Ministry of Agriculture says offshore fishing moratorium is being enforced between July 1 and November 31.
- Shanghai is to require all cars to use unleaded petrol by the end of this year.
- Vice-Premier Zhu Rongji urges government officials to buy grain at protective prices.
